system.summary: IFN-γ acts through a receptor–JAK1/JAK2–STAT1 axis. Its best-characterised transcriptional output in macrophages is a fast primary wave that includes IRF1 and SOCS1, followed by IFN-γ-inducible chemokines, CXCL9 and CXCL10 among them. In the intent's effective model, the unobserved activity A stands for this STAT1-dependent (and possibly IRF1-assisted) transcriptional activity, and each transcript is a basal-plus-A-driven production balanced by first-order decay. JAK–STAT signalling is known to be self-limiting. SOCS1 is induced by IFN-γ and is a critical inhibitor of IFN-γ signalling in mice. Other negative regulators (tyrosine phosphatases, PIAS proteins) are also described. So an attenuation of A is biologically plausible, but not specific to SOCS1. The dataset (Xue et al. 2014, GEO GSE46903) has these facts: one IFN-γ dose (200 IU/ml), baseline cells differentiated for 72 h in GM-CSF, and log2 quantile-normalised Illumina intensities with a dataset-wide background of 6.747 log2. Gene-specific mRNA half-lives for IRF1, SOCS1, CXCL9 and CXCL10 in human GM-CSF macrophages are not known to me from a checkable source.
system.scope: Protocol and assay facts come from the study itself: human CD14+ monocyte-derived macrophages, 72 h GM-CSF, IFN-γ 200 IU/ml, Illumina HT-12 V3 (supplied papers lit_1–lit_3). Pathway and feedback facts come from reviews covering mouse and human cells (mostly macrophages, fibroblasts and cell lines) and from mouse SOCS1-knockout experiments. mRNA decay-rate facts come from mouse cells (NIH3T3 fibroblasts; mouse cells under inflammatory stimuli), not from human macrophages under IFN-γ.
unknowns: Whether IFN-γ stayed in the medium for the whole interval, and whether the medium was changed or GM-CSF was still present at t = 0, is not stated by the study.
Whether the deposited GEO VALUEs include the batch-effect removal described in the supplement is not known.
mRNA half-lives of IRF1, SOCS1, CXCL9 and CXCL10 in human GM-CSF macrophages, basal or IFN-γ-stimulated, are not known from a checkable source.
What drives the transient CXCL10 (and SOCS1) rise in untreated controls at 6–12 h is unknown. Culture handling or autocrine signalling are possibilities, not established.

Whether attenuation of IFN-γ transcriptional activity in human macrophages is dominated by SOCS1 or by other negative regulators (phosphatases, PIAS, receptor down-regulation, ligand depletion) is not settled for this system.
Whether CXCL9/CXCL10 induction depends on newly made IRF1 protein (a second tier), rather than only on the primary STAT1 activity, is not resolved for this system.

notes:
Offline, no tools: the reply rests on my own knowledge plus the three supplied papers. No searches were run, and I did not read the cited documents in this session. Non-supplied items are cited by DOI only where I am confident of the identifier, and they carry no quotes. The supports statements are deliberately limited to the central claims of those papers.

The quotes on lit_1–lit_3 are the ones supplied with those items.

Not found, or not citable with a sure identifier:
- gene-specific mRNA half-lives of IRF1, SOCS1, CXCL9 and CXCL10 in human macrophages;
- a time-resolved measurement of STAT1 activity attenuation in human GM-CSF macrophages under continuous IFN-γ;
- a primary source on whether CXCL9/CXCL10 induction requires IRF1 protein in this system;
- published effective mechanistic models of IFN-γ–STAT1–SOCS1 feedback. Such models exist (e.g. Yamada et al. 2003, FEBS Lett), but I am not sure of the identifier, so it is not cited.

The degradation evidence (req_2, req_4, req_6, req_8) supports first-order mRNA decay only as a general principle from mouse cells, not these transcripts in this system.

Hypothesis structure (inference_target is mechanism_discrimination):
- The base is the essential set: -> A [IFNg], A ->, and req_1–req_8.
- H_SOCS1 adds SOCS1_act (-> SOCS1_act [SOCS1_mRNA], SOCS1_act ->) and replaces -> A [IFNg] with -> A [IFNg, SOCS1_act].
- H_ATT is the same with R produced from A.
- A further alternative, decline of the effective stimulus (ligand depletion), would change the condition encoding against the working assumption. It is given as a fact, not a reaction, because IFNg is an input.
- The literature shows SOCS1 inhibits IFN-γ signalling, but also that other negative regulators exist. Discriminating H_SOCS1 from H_ATT on four mRNAs alone may not be possible, since both predict attenuation of A; the SOCS1_mRNA-driven variant differs only in the shape of the inhibitor's time course.

On the data source: the lab note cites GEO GSE46903 but names the raw file GSE47189_family.soft. I believe GSE46903 is a SuperSeries containing the HT-12 V3 subseries, but I have not verified the accession relationship.
